I hated the theatrical cut. I wasn't expecting the Ultimate Edition to be able to do such a good job of salvaging the movie. The ultimate edition is much more coherent.

Don't get me wrong. It's still got serious issues. The numerous dream sequences, while visually enjoyable and at least in one instance touching, are never explained within the context of the film itself. It's awkward and jarring. The cartoony CGI version of Doomsday is laughably bad. Lex Luthor's ultimate reason for his actions is that while he's incredibly brilliant, he's simply crazy. The Martha shit is still glaringly stupid. "Your mom's name is Martha? That's my mom's name! I suddenly feel remorse for my actions because you said a thing that reminds me of myself! I guess I'm not going to kill you now." I suppose there was no way to salvage that one.

But my biggest gripe of all is that heroes aren't heroes in this universe. They're petty self-righteous thugs who steal, stalk, intimidate, mutilate, and murder. The only things that separate them from the rest of the people are their abilities, and they are not at all responsible in the way they use those abilities. They simply do whatever they want, which ultimately makes their conflicts nothing more than selfish squabbles between dangerous, out of control, deluded prima donna assholes. To be fair, I think that's at least partially a result of the movie taking itself too seriously.

Is the movie still enjoyable? In spite of its flaws, yes. It is. The ultimate edition is a huge improvement over the theatrical cut. If you hated this movie as much as me, you should definitely give the ultimate edition a chance.
